Let $f(x)=x^{3}-3 x^{2}+2$ be a function defined on $(-1,3]$.

Which of the following statements is/are correct?

  1. $f(x)$ has exactly two roots in $[-0.9,0]$.
  2. $f(x)$ has a minimum at $2$ only.
  3. $f(x)$ has maximum at $0$ only.
  4. $f(x)$ has a root at $1$.
questions.explanation: \[ f(x) = x^3 - 3x^2 + 2, \quad x \in (-1,3]. \] 1) Roots of f(x) Method 1: Direct factorization Check x = 1: \[ f(1) = 1 - 3 + 2 = 0. \] So, 1 is a root. Factorizing: \[ f(x) = (x-1)(x^2 - 2x - 2). \] Solve: \[ x^2 - 2x - 2 = 0. \] \[ x = 1 \pm \sqrt{3}. \] Approximate roots: \[ 1-\sqrt{3} \approx -0.732, \quad 1, \quad 1+\sqrt{3} \approx 2.732. \] In the interval [-0.9,0], only one root \[ -0.732 \] exists. Method 2: Using Intermediate Value Theorem (IVT) Since f(x) is a polynomial, it is continuous on [-0.9,0]. Check signs: \[ f(-0.9) = -1.159 < 0 \] \[ f(0) = 2 > 0 \] Since the function changes sign, \[ f(-0.9)\cdot f(0) < 0, \] by the Intermediate Value Theorem, there exists at least one root in (-0.9,0). Note: Opposite signs guarantee at least one root, but not necessarily exactly one root. $$ 1 + \frac{1}{3^2} + \frac{1}{5^2} + \frac{1}{7^2} + \cdots \text { is }$$
